flashcards.q: What is the Factory Method pattern?
flashcards.a: A creational pattern that provides an interface for creating objects, but lets SUBCLASSES decide which class to instantiate.

flashcards.q: What is Factory Method also known as?
flashcards.a: Virtual Constructor.

flashcards.q: What is the key principle of Factory Method?
flashcards.a: 'Don't call us, we'll call you' - The framework calls your factory method when it needs an object.

flashcards.q: What are the 4 participants in Factory Method pattern?
flashcards.a: 1) Product (interface), 2) ConcreteProduct (implements Product), 3) Creator (declares factory method), 4) ConcreteCreator (overrides factory method).

flashcards.q: When should you use Factory Method?
flashcards.a: When you don't know exact types beforehand, want to provide framework extension points, or want to localize object creation logic.

flashcards.q: When should you NOT use Factory Method?
flashcards.a: For simple object creation where you always know the type, or when you need families of related objects (use Abstract Factory instead).

flashcards.q: How does Factory Method differ from Simple Factory?
flashcards.a: Factory Method uses inheritance with subclass hierarchy. Simple Factory is just one class with switch statement - not a design pattern, just an idiom.

flashcards.q: How does Factory Method differ from Abstract Factory?
flashcards.a: Factory Method: creates ONE type of product using inheritance. Abstract Factory: creates FAMILIES of related products using composition with multiple factory methods.

flashcards.q: How does Factory Method differ from Builder?
flashcards.a: Factory Method focuses on WHICH object to create (simple creation). Builder focuses on HOW to construct complex objects step-by-step.

flashcards.q: What is Parameterized Factory Method?
flashcards.a: A variation where factory method accepts parameters to determine which product type to create (often uses switch statement).

flashcards.q: What is Lazy Initialization in Factory Method?
flashcards.a: A variation where products are created only when first needed, not upfront.

flashcards.q: What is the Registry Pattern variation?
flashcards.a: Products are registered dynamically at runtime into a map/registry, and factory looks up the product class by type key.

flashcards.q: What SOLID principles does Factory Method support?
flashcards.a: 1) Single Responsibility - creation code isolated. 2) Open/Closed - add new products without modifying existing code.

flashcards.q: What pattern often works hand-in-hand with Factory Method?
flashcards.a: Template Method - the creator's template method uses the factory method internally, hiding it from clients.

flashcards.q: Name 3 real-world examples of Factory Method.
flashcards.a: 1) React's createElement(), 2) Node.js fs.createReadStream/WriteStream, 3) Express middleware factories (express.json()).

flashcards.q: Why is Factory Method essential for framework design?
flashcards.a: It allows framework to define the workflow but lets users extend it by implementing their own concrete creators and products.

flashcards.q: What is a common pitfall with Factory Method?
flashcards.a: Overusing it - don't create factories for simple object creation where direct instantiation works fine.

flashcards.q: What should a factory method focus on?
flashcards.a: Only creation. Keep factory methods simple - don't add initialization, validation, setup, or connection logic.

flashcards.q: What is Static Factory Method?
flashcards.a: A variation where factory method is static (class method) - simpler but loses ability to override in subclasses.

flashcards.q: What are the main disadvantages of Factory Method?
flashcards.a: Code complexity (many subclasses), inheritance-based (not composition), indirection makes code harder to follow.
